tldr: Best overall: spring (Apr–May) and autumn (Sep–Nov) — mild and comfortable.
Summer (Jun–Aug) is hot and humid with a rainy monsoon; pack light + an umbrella.
Winter (Dec–Feb) is cold and dry; bring a warm coat and layers.
Cherry-blossom and fall-foliage timing shifts every year — check that year's forecast.

highlights.title: Spring & autumn are the sweet spots
highlights.body: Mild temperatures, lower humidity and big scenery: cherry blossoms in spring, fiery foliage in autumn. These are peak travel seasons, so book accommodation early.

highlights.title: Summer = heat + monsoon
highlights.body: June–August is hot and humid, with a rainy monsoon stretch (usually late June–July) and occasional late-summer typhoons. Breathable clothes and a compact umbrella are essential.

highlights.title: Winter is cold but bright
highlights.body: December–February is cold and dry, with Seoul often below freezing and some snow. Indoor heating is strong, so dress in layers you can peel off.

seasons.title: The four seasons, and what to pack

cards.name: Spring
cards.vibe: Mild, cherry blossoms, occasional fine dust.
cards.pack: Light layers, a light jacket, and a mask on high fine-dust days.

cards.name: Summer
cards.vibe: Hot, humid, monsoon rain, some typhoons.
cards.pack: Breathable clothes, a compact umbrella, sunscreen, and a layer for strong AC.

cards.name: Autumn
cards.vibe: Crisp, clear and dry — prime hiking and foliage.
cards.pack: Light layers and a warmer jacket for late autumn.

cards.name: Winter
cards.vibe: Cold and dry, Seoul below freezing, some snow.
cards.pack: A warm coat, hat/gloves, and layers for strong indoor heating.

items.d: Roughly late March to mid-April, earlier in the warmer south (Jeju/Busan) than in Seoul. Exact dates move each year — follow that year's blossom forecast.
Usually mid-October to early November, starting in the mountains and north and moving south. Check the current-year foliage forecast.
A rainy stretch, generally late June into July. Trips are still fine — just plan indoor options and carry rain gear.
Air quality can dip in spring (and at times winter). Check an air-quality app; wear a mask on bad days.
Cherry-blossom and foliage peaks shift by a week or more each year. Don't lock non-refundable plans to a fixed date — track the forecast.
Late June–July can bring heavy rain. Pack a real umbrella/rain jacket and have indoor backups.
It's not just hot — it's humid. Hydrate, plan midday indoor breaks, and dress for strong indoor air-conditioning.
Seoul winters bite. A proper coat, plus a layer for very warm indoor heating, beats one thick jumper.
On high fine-dust days, a mask and fewer strenuous outdoor plans make a real difference.

items.q: When is the best time to visit Korea?
items.a: Spring (April–May) and autumn (September–November) are the most comfortable — mild, drier and scenic. They're also the busiest, so book early.

items.q: When do the cherry blossoms bloom?
items.a: Roughly late March to mid-April, earlier in the south. The exact peak shifts each year, so follow that year's blossom forecast rather than a fixed date.

items.q: Is summer a bad time to go?
items.a: It's hot, humid and has a rainy monsoon (late June–July), but it's far from a write-off — just pack light, carry an umbrella and plan some indoor time.
Seoul is often below freezing in December–February, with some snow. It's cold and dry; a warm coat and layers handle it, and indoor heating is strong.
Fine dust (미세먼지) is airborne particulate pollution that can rise in spring and at times winter. Check an air-quality app and wear a mask on bad days.
